means: The medium itself - Japanese commercial animation drawing convention: large eyes, simplified noses, flat cel colour, a black keyline.
does: Very little here, because it is already the model default. animagine-xl-4.0 is an anime SDXL trained on danbooru; asking it for anime is asking water to be wet. The tag does not make a frame more anime, it spends a token. The reliable way to hold the medium on this box runs the other direction - push the competing media OUT through the negative prompt, which is what craft/ANIME_MODELS.md does with 'photorealistic, 3d, western comic'.
reach_for_it: only as a counterweight, when a photographic or live-action noun in the subject line is dragging the render off-medium and you want something in the positive pushing back
used_in: implicit in every render on this box; the explicit word appears only inside compound style phrases such as 'modern sports anime'
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
